🔥🇲🇽 <u>Honda fired him for organizing in 2011. Today he goes back in.</u>

José Luis Solorio was fired for union organizing at Honda's El Salto plant in Jalisco, then jailed on charges later proven false. The employer-controlled labor board took 15 years to rule in his favor. Honda filed an amparo to block his return, but the STPS set his reinstatement for November 12, 2026. Independent unions see it as a test of whether the post-2019 labor regime protects organizers once they're back on the shop floor.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>WikiLeaks cable: IFE official told the US Embassy the quick count could be withheld if AMLO lost by 3% or less</u>

A US Embassy cable published by La Jornada says IFE electoral councillor Arturo Sánchez Gutiérrez told American diplomats, 18 days before the 2006 vote, that the institute might not announce the quick count if López Obrador lost by 3 points or less. That is what happened on July 2. The embassy also wrote that he "clearly has little regard" for AMLO. Sheinbaum: the IFE has "at least one terrible stain, the 2006 electoral fraud," and now the opposition "is trying to discredit the 2027 election."

🇲🇽🏥 <u>IMSS-Bienestar: 118,000 health workers get permanent posts, 19,314 new hires</u>

Starting January 1, 2027, IMSS-Bienestar will give 118,038 health workers permanent positions, including 21,941 on temporary contracts "in precarious conditions." It will hire 19,314 specialists, nurses and residents, about 3,000 of them before November 30. Through Médicos por México, 78 mobile surgical teams will cover the system's 296 rural hospitals, with a target of more than 16,000 surgeries in 120 days. Five teams are already working in Chiapas.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Foreign Minister Velasco heads to Tokyo as Mexico widens its map</u>

Foreign Minister Roberto Velasco is in Japan to meet Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi, Japanese investors and Mexican scientists, and to launch the Mexican Chamber of Commerce in Japan. More than 1,600 Japanese companies already operate in Mexico, employing nearly 350,000 people. The trip comes days before Sheinbaum flies to APEC in Shenzhen.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Mexico expects a steel, aluminum and auto tariff deal with the US before 2027</u>

Deputy Economy Secretary Luis Rosendo Gutiérrez says a deal on the Section 232 tariffs is expected before the year ends. Around 80% of Mexican exports already enter the US tariff-free. Mexico didn't just wait on Washington: 55% of its trade-defense cases now target unfair steel imports, IMMEX permits with irregularities were cancelled, and antidumping duties now hit hot-rolled steel from China and Vietnam.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>MEXICO'S AUTO-PARTS INDUSTRY SETS AN ALL-TIME MONTHLY RECORD</u>

Mexico produced $11.118 billion in auto parts in August, a record for any single month and 8.53% more than in August 2025, according to the National Auto Parts Industry (INA), as reported by El Economista. January–August output reached $85.82 billion, up 8.31%, and the sector ran a $24.566 billion trade surplus. INA's Julio Galván credits North American regional content and "the substitution of imports from Asian countries," which is driving the growth of domestic suppliers.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>MEXICO IS BACK AT THE UN CLIMATE SUMMIT WITH ITS OWN PAVILION, THE FIRST IN 12+ YEARS</u>

At COP31 in Antalya, Turkey (November 9–20), the Semarnat–SRE delegation is presenting ADAPTA MX 1.0, Mexico's first National Climate Change Adaptation Policy. It came out of seven regional workshops and pairs a climate-risk diagnosis with 33 adaptation measures against drought and torrential rain, including integrated water management, early-warning systems and resilient infrastructure. Mexico and Poland will also co-facilitate the ministerial consultations on a just transition.

🇲🇽⚓ <u>NAVY PUTS 1,300 PERSONNEL ON MICHOACÁN'S COCAINE SEA ROUTE</u>

Navy Secretary Adm. Raymundo Pedro Morales Ángeles said maritime trafficking routes carrying drugs "mainly from Colombia, Ecuador and South American countries" are one of the main threats, with Cárteles Unidos, the CJNG and the Sinaloa Cartel landing loads on the Michoacán coast, near the port of Lázaro Cárdenas, and moving them on to central and northern Mexico and the United States. Semar now has 1,300 personnel there: seven ocean-going ships guarding waters out to 200 nautical miles, three coastal ships, nine interceptor boats, two long-range drones, two helicopters and 61 vehicles in Lázaro Cárdenas, Coahuayana and Aquila.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>SHEINBAUM ON FOBAPROA: "WHO PAID? THE PEOPLE. WE ARE STILL PAYING"</u>

Asked about the collapse of Paraguay's Ueno Bank, President Sheinbaum pointed to Mexico's own 1994 bank rescue, which turned the private debts of a group of bankers and businessmen into public debt. She said the bailout was riddled with corruption, with some companies receiving more than they needed to stay afloat, and announced her government will present material from AMLO's book on Fobaproa that names the people and firms that benefited improperly. "A people without memory loses its compass."

🇲🇽🔬 <u>SHEINBAUM OPENS THREE PERMANENT FUNDS FOR YOUNG SCIENTISTS</u>

At the National Meeting of Science Students at the SEP, President Sheinbaum announced three permanent calls: travel and lodging for students who compete in national and international contests, an initial 100-million-peso fund for projects of up to 100,000 pesos each, and full coverage of the cost of registering patents and trademarks. La Escuela es Nuestra will also get a bigger budget to equip high-school laboratories. She handed out 132 awards to students from across the country.
